_comment: Lifecycle + event callbacks of a Lua module table / Python horizon.Behavior subclass. Lua names come from ScriptEngine.cpp (pushInstanceMethod), Python names from PyScriptBackend.cpp (PyObject_CallMethod). 'to' = who receives it: 'entity' = only the instance on the entity concerned, 'all' = every text-script instance in the session. gen_reference.py checks both name lists against the source.

items.when: Once, when the script starts: at the start of play mode, in a packaged game when its scene loads, and for scripts on entities that arrive later (an additive zone). Exposed properties are already set.
Every frame. dt is the scaled frame time in seconds (0 while the game is paused through horizon.time.setTimeScale(0)).

groups.title: Physics contacts
groups.note: Both entities of a contact get the event, each with the other's id. A contact where either side no longer exists is dropped entirely. A trigger contact fires both pairs: onCollisionEnter and onBeginOverlap, then onCollisionExit and onEndOverlap.

items.when: Another physics body starts touching this entity.
It stops touching.
Something enters a trigger collider on this entity, or this entity enters one.
The overlap ends.

groups.title: Input actions
groups.note: Actions are the ones defined in the project's input mapping. These go to every script instance, not only to the player's entity; pick the action by name. For polling instead of events use horizon.input.actionDown and friends.

items.when: A button action went down this frame.
A button action went up this frame.
Every frame, for each 1D axis action, with its current value (not multiplied by dt).
Every frame, for each 2D axis action. Note the lower-case d in the Python name.

A timer started with horizon.timer.after or horizon.timer.every went off. handle is the value those calls returned; compare it to tell your timers apart, because every instance receives every timer. Timers run on real time, a paused game does not stretch them.
The entity's animation passed a single-frame notify called name.
A notify state (a notify with a duration) started.
The notify state ended.

groups.title: In-game UI pointer
groups.note: Sent to scripts on entities with an interactive UI element (a button, or any element carrying a script) under the mouse.

items.when: The element was clicked: pressed and released over it.
The pointer moved onto the element.
The pointer left it.

groups.title: Multiplayer session
groups.note: Every script instance on the machine concerned receives these. Each event happens on one side only: the host hears players come and go, a client hears its own connection. Measured with host and client in Lua and Python.

items.when: Client only: the connection is up and the host's world has arrived (net.status() is 3). A client gets no onSessionStarted.

Client only: the host is gone or removed us; the status is now 4. reason: 0 left, 1 connection lost, 2 kicked, 3 refused, 4 other engine version, 5 other project. A kick with anti-cheat off arrives as 1. Not sent for a leave() of our own, and not followed by onSessionEnded.
Host only: a player joined and has the world. player is their player number (2, 3, …), the one net.playerName takes, not an anti-cheat connection number.
Host only: a player left, was kicked or timed out. net.playerName(player) is already empty.
Host only: net.host opened a session.
net.leave() ended the session on this machine, on the host also when hosting again. Not sent to a client that was removed or lost the host (that is onDisconnected).

A replicated variable (declared with horizon.net.declareVarInt and its siblings) arrived with a new value on this client. Never called on the host, which set the value itself. <var> is the variable's name verbatim (health gives onRep_health / on_rep_health); old is the previous value: in Python a list [x, y, z] for a Vector, in Lua the number 0 for a Vector (known issue). Read the new one with horizon.net.getVarInt and its siblings. Only on the entity whose variable changed, and only for variables declared with notify. A client that wrote the variable itself gets it again when the host's value comes back.

A remote call from horizon.net.callServer, callClient or callAllClients runs the method of exactly that name on the target entity's script, with the caller's extra arguments. No renaming between languages: a Lua takeDamage is reached by a Python caller as takeDamage. On the host the method runs only for a call from a client: offline and on the host itself these rows reach a HorizonCode class only, see Remote calls.

The host's anti-cheat filed a report. Read it with horizon.anticheat.reportLevel, reportRule, reportPlayer … and override the host's reaction with horizon.anticheat.respond in the same frame. On a client it fires once, when the host is removing it (reportPlayer 0). Never fires in build 7d49d44f, see Anti-Cheat.
